newsitem.title: USA: Virginia Port Auth. $38 mln bonds rated AA - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: Virginia Port Auth. $38 mln bonds rated AA - Fitch.

text.p: NEW YORK, Oct 15 - Virginia Port Authority's $38.3 million commonwealth port fund revenue bonds, series 1996, are rated 'AA' by Fitch Investors Service.

The bonds are expected Oct. 22, 1996 through negotiation with a syndicate led by Wheat First Butcher Singer. Furthermore, $24,085,000 of the bonds will be due serially July 1, 1998-2011 and $14,215,000 will be term bonds with mandatory sinking fund redemption due July 1, 2016. Bonds will be optionally callable beginning July 1, 2006 at 101%. The rating on the port fund bonds reflects the credit of Virginia, whose general obligation bonds are rated 'AAA'. The revenues appropriated to the securing port fund represent general revenues of the commonwealth.

These bonds are not general obligations of either the commonwealth or the port authority. Security for these port fund bonds, on a parity with the outstanding $80.03 million, series 1988, bonds, also rated 'AA', emanates from monthly set-asides to the credit of the Port Fund, a dedicated, non-reverting fund within the commonwealth's broad transportation trust fund. Such amounts are derived from the 1986-enacted increases to the sales tax, the motor vehicle sales and use tax, motor fuel tax and motor vehicle registration fees -- 4.2% of such additional revenues are allocated for port purposes (the remainder is allocated for highways, mass transportation and airports). In fiscal 1996, port fund primary income, absent interest earnings, amounted to $22.6 million, providing about 1.6 times coverage of estimated maximum debt service on these and the outstanding parity bonds. While in the past the commonwealth's general fund has made appropriations to the port authority for the bulk of debt service, thus freeing port operating revenues for purposes associated with the enterprise, it is intended that beginning in the current fiscal year, the port fund operating revenues supplant the commonwealth's general fund support. The authority is responsible for the very extensive port facilities in the Hampton Roads Harbor region, as well as an inland port. The facilities are operated by the Virginia International Terminals, Inc. (VIT), a Virginia non-stock, non-profit private corporation. Pursuant to an operating agreement, VIT makes monthly transfers to the authority for operating expenses, debt service and capital purposes. Hampton Roads, the second largest of the east coast ports, handled 9.6 million short tons of general cargo in 1995, up about 30% from 1993, and is a major contributor to the economy of Virginia. The commonwealth is integrally involved in its operations.
